title: Beyond Urban Regret: A Critical Perspective on the Adaptive Reuse of Wasted Spaces in Traditional Morphology
content: Historic urban settlements in Oman face increasing challenges associated with residential migration, deteriorating infrastructure, inadequate public amenities, and the loss of traditional urban identity. This study investigates the adaptive reuse potential of underutilized urban spaces within Al-Sahel, a historic district of Sur, Oman, to support community-oriented regeneration while preserving its traditional morphology. Employing a mixed-methods approach, the research integrates community surveys, field observations, spatial mapping, and AI-assisted design visualization to assess existing urban conditions and identify regeneration opportunities. The findings reveal that 93,124 m², representing 22.44% of the study area, comprises underutilized spaces. Five distinct spatial typologies were identified: coastal voids, transitional building setbacks, circulation corridors, enclosed communal courtyards, and hybrid large-scale nodes. Survey findings highlight residents' concerns regarding inadequate recreational spaces, deteriorating infrastructure, and limited accessibility. Based on these findings, context-sensitive adaptive reuse scenarios were developed to illustrate potential improvements in pedestrian connectivity, public amenities, and community interaction. Although implementation requires further technical and regulatory assessment, the study demonstrates how targeted urban acupuncture strategies can inform sustainable regeneration while maintaining the cultural and morphological identity of historic Omani settlements.
